channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Dividido, STF tem decisões polêmicas pela frente com poder de influenciar o ano eleitoral e o inquérito do Master
item.description: The Supreme Federal Court (STF) faces controversial decisions that could deepen internal divisions, influence the 2026 electoral landscape, and impact the Banco Master investigation, particularly through the review of the imprisonment of Daniel Vorcaro’s relatives and the potential plea bargain by the banker. The Court is also reviewing changes to the Clean Record Law that could benefit ineligible politicians such as Eduardo Cunha and José Roberto Arruda, and determining the future of the Rio de Janeiro election after Cláudio Castro’s resignation. The acceptance or rejection of Vorcaro’s new plea deal by the Federal Police and PGR this week may have direct repercussions on the presidential campaign, especially against Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: Nova proposta de delação de Vorcaro ainda não trouxe elementos inéditos, avaliam investigadores
item.description: Federal Police and Prosecutor's Office investigators assess that Daniel Vorcaro's new plea bargain proposal did not introduce novel elements to change the case's perception. The submitted material mentions payments to Senator Ciro Nogueira and the film 'Dark Horse', but is seen as redundant and used as justification. The defense has until this week to add new information before Supreme Court Justice André Mendonça rules on the agreement's homologation.

item.title: Em 20 anos, Brasil ganhou quase 33 milhões de eleitores
item.description: Over the past 20 years, Brazil has gained nearly 33 million voters, increasing from 125.9 million in 2006 to 158.9 million in 2026, a total rise of 26.17%. The country has added an average of 1.6 million voters per year, equivalent to an annual growth rate of 1.1%. The figures compare the 2006 general elections, won by Lula, with the upcoming 2026 elections.

item.title: Flávio intensifica disputas no TSE enquanto PT segue indefinido
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro’s (PL-RJ) pre-campaign is intensifying its legal offensive at the TSE with over 40 electoral representations against Lula and the PT, led by former TSE minister Maria Cláudia Bucchianeri as legal coordinator. Meanwhile, the PT has yet to formalize its legal coordination for the TSE, despite Lula’s preference for Marco Aurélio de Carvalho, causing internal discomfort due to Edinho Silva’s hesitation to confirm the appointment. As of June 2, the PL had responded to 23 representations filed by the PT and other parties, totaling 67 actions related to the 2026 elections.

item.title: Semana tem PEC da 6 X 1, julgamento sobre big techs e Copa
item.description: This week, Senate President Davi Alcolumbre is expected to set the pace for the PEC ending the 6x1 work schedule, with potential multi-committee review making approval before the July recess unlikely. Meanwhile, the STF is reviewing cases on the Marco Civil da Internet, addressing platform liability for user-generated content and the admissibility of evidence in sexual crimes cases. Economically, Middle East tensions between Israel and Iran are pressuring markets, while IBGE will release May's IPCA, forecast at 0.5%, below April's 0.67%.

item.title: Governo Lula estuda 2º funcionário para MEI depois do fim da 6 X 1
item.description: The Lula government is studying allowing MEI (Microentrepreneur Individual) to hire a second employee as compensation for the end of the 6x1 work schedule, which will increase costs for small businesses. The proposal, still under analysis, aims to be fiscally sustainable and prioritizes the commerce sector, most affected by the change. Minister Paulo Pereira stated no decision has been made and that Sebrae is involved in designing a support program for adaptation.

item.title: PoderData: 47% dos eleitores veem piora da corrupção sob Lula
item.description: According to a PoderData survey conducted from May to June 2026, 47% of Brazilians believe corruption has increased under President Lula’s government, compared to 21% who see a decrease and 28% who see no change. The perception of increased corruption declined by 2 points since January 2026, while the perception of decreased corruption rose by 3 points. The survey, with a 2-point margin of error, included 2,500 interviews nationwide and took place amid controversies such as the Banco Master case and alleged ties between Lula’s relatives and figures under investigation.

item.title: Governo Lula estuda elevar teto do MEI para até R$ 130 mil
item.description: The Lula government is studying raising the MEI's annual revenue cap from R$ 81,000 to up to R$ 130,000, with a formal proposal being prepared by the Ministry of Entrepreneurship. The change, unlikely in 2025 due to budgetary and electoral constraints, also includes allowing a second employee and measures to prevent fraud such as 'sideways growth'.

item.title: Entre quem diz saber do caso Master, 48% culpam governo Lula
item.description: 48% of Brazilians aware of the Banco Master case blame the Lula government for allowing irregularities, while 32% blame the Bolsonaro administration. The case, involving banking fraud, money laundering, and alleged payments to finance a Bolsonaro biopic, is being politicized by both sides ahead of the 2026 elections. Investigations reveal contacts between the bank’s founder and figures from both political camps, making it difficult for either side to fully distance itself.

item.title: Lula acena a entregadores jovens com crédito para moto
item.description: The Lula government is preparing Move Motos, a subsidized credit line for app-based delivery workers to purchase motorcycles, with launch expected by June 2026. The initiative aims to strengthen ties with young male workers in the Southeast—a demographic where Lula has below-average approval—by replacing labor regulation efforts with financial incentives. The program will be a new branch of Move Brasil, with funding below the R$ 30 billion allocated for cars used by ride-hailing and taxi drivers.

item.title: Oposição tem 19 assinaturas por CPI do Master na Alesp, diz autor do pedido
item.description: State deputy Guilherme Cortez (PSOL-SP) said the opposition has gathered 19 of the 23 signatures needed to request a CPI in Alesp to investigate alleged links between Banco Master and São Paulo municipalities, including the capital. The request could also reach the state government, as Fabiano Zettel — brother-in-law of Daniel Vorcaro and identified by the PF as a Master case operator — donated R$ 2 million to Tarcísio de Freitas’ campaign. Cortez added that privatizations, especially of Sabesp, will be a central issue in Fernando Haddad’s (PT) campaign for governor of SP.

item.title: Podcast analisa relação de Flávio Bolsonaro com evangélicos após caso Dark Horse
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) participated in the March for Jesus in São Paulo, using the event to reinforce an electoral discourse rooted in spiritual warfare narratives and the promise to expel 'evil' from government. His remarks on Thursday (4) frame the 2026 election as a moral and religious confrontation, aligning with the evangelical base following the Dark Horse case. The tone is overtly campaign-oriented, blending religious rhetoric with political messaging.

item.title: PEC da Liberdade ou Escravidão? O que pode mudar no regime de trabalho por hora proposto por Flávio Bolsonaro para barrar fim da 6x1
item.description: The 'PEC da Liberdade,' proposed by Flávio Bolsonaro and Rogério Marinho, aims to replace the 6x1 work schedule with an hourly work regime, allowing workers to choose between traditional CLT and a flexible model, with pay proportional to hours worked and individual agreements taking precedence over collective ones. Critics label it the 'PEC da Escravidão,' warning it could enable exploitative schedules like 7x0 without weekly rest, arguing it favors employers by weakening collective bargaining.

item.title: A crítica de Lula a Moraes em conversa com dois ministros do STF
item.description: Lula expressed dissatisfaction with Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes for blocking the nomination of Jorge Messias to the STF, according to his allies. The criticism was made in a private conversation with two other STF ministers. The incident highlights ongoing tension between the Planalto and the Judiciary over Supreme Court appointments.

item.title: Governadores aumentam gastos, e estados devem somar déficit de R$ 6 bi no ano eleitoral
item.description: Brazilian states are projected to record a fiscal deficit of R$ 6 billion in 2026, according to XP Investments, reversing the R$ 6.6 billion surplus achieved in 2025. This deterioration in state public accounts occurs during the election year, following a trend similar to that seen in federal finances. The article, exclusive to subscribers, highlights the impact of increased spending by governors.

item.title: Copa do Mundo abre janela de oportunidade para a pré-campanha
item.description: Brazil's victory over Egypt in a pre-World Cup friendly sparked intense debate on social media and WhatsApp groups, highlighting goals by Bruno Guimarães and Endrick, a defensive lapse by Marquinhos, and the absence of Rayan despite his recent goal against Panama. The engagement during the match signals that the upcoming World Cup will serve as a major platform to capture Brazilians' attention over the next 40 days, presenting a strategic opportunity to launch or boost pre-election campaigns.

item.title: Artigo: terceira via é espécie de Peter Pan tropical
item.description: The article analyzes how Lula's government measures — such as abolishing the 'blusinhas' tax, subsidizing new cars for app and taxi drivers, and the Desenrola Brasil 2 program — while well-received and having high recall, are not significantly shifting voter intent. They are seen as temporary relief, insufficient to address structural problems, arriving 'out of timing' and perceived by some voters as electoral acts rather than state policies. Nevertheless, the cumulative effect of these small actions is currently favoring the government in a 'work in progress' scenario.

item.title: Entrevista: Lula vai ter mais de um palanque em vários estados para aproximar o centro, diz Wellington Dias
item.description: Minister Wellington Dias says Lula’s 2026 re-election campaign must build state-level slates to broaden center-right support, emphasizing dialogue with Senate President Davi Alcolumbre to secure governability. He acknowledges Lula’s third term failed to gain a simple congressional majority due to neglected alliances and defends renominating Jorge Messias to the STF as a presidential right achievable through negotiation.

item.title: Governo Lula espera reunião com representante de Comércio dos EUA nesta semana para discutir tarifaço
item.description: The Lula government plans to hold a videoconference this week with U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer to discuss new U.S. tariffs on Brazilian goods. The meeting will include Ministers Marcio Elias Rosa (Industry and Trade) and Mauro Vieira (Foreign Affairs), as part of the working group established during the May 7 White House meeting between Lula and Trump. Vieira stated the U.S. justifications for tariffs are illegitimate and emphasized Brazil’s commitment to continued dialogue, despite allegations concerning Pix, intellectual property, deforestation, and forced labor.

item.title: Comissão da Câmara vota redução da maioridade penal e amplia pressão sobre o governo na segurança pública
item.description: The Chamber’s Constitution and Justice Committee is set to vote on Tuesday on a constitutional amendment to lower the age of criminal responsibility from 18 to 16, a measure backed by the opposition and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro to pressure the government on public security. While the government is divided — with the Justice Minister supporting debate but not automatic reduction — PT deputies warn the change could lead to further lowering of the age and early recruitment of youth by organized crime.

item.title: Flávio lança jingle com funk e diz que “Pix é do Bolsonaro”
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) released an AI-generated campaign jingle in funk style claiming that Pix was created by his father, Jair Bolsonaro, with the lyric 'Pix is Bolsonaro's, my love'. The video shows the former president dancing with a pandeiro and both wearing shirts bearing the slogan, reinforcing the narrative that Pix is a family legacy immune to external pressures, particularly following U.S. threats of 25% tariffs over concerns it harms Visa and Mastercard.

item.title: ELEIÇÕES 2026: Flávio Bolsonaro Será o Próximo Presidente? A Virada Que Ninguém Viu Chegar
item.description: The provided content does not contain any relevant information about the 2026 elections or Flávio Bolsonaro as a presidential candidate. It consists solely of generic YouTube interface messages, such as instructions to unmute, links, watch history notes, and playback errors, with no mention of any political figure, campaign, polling data, or Brazilian political context.

item.title: Em meio ao embate com o governo, Flávio lança jingle com funk criado por IA que diz que 'Pix é do Bolsonaro'
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) released an AI-generated funk jingle claiming that the Pix payment system was created by his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, in response to the Lula government reviving the slogan 'Pix is ours'. The clip, part of a 2026 election strategy, ties the payment method to Bolsonaro’s legacy and alleges opponents seek to take it away, using AI-generated visuals showing Pix in daily use.

item.title: O Atlas da Violência trouxe boas notícias para Zema e Caiado
item.description: The 2026 Violence Atlas revealed the lowest homicide count in Brazil since 2014, with significant declines in Goiás and Minas Gerais. Former governors Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) and Romeu Zema (Novo) celebrated these results, attributing them to their public security policies during their tenures. Caiado reduced Goiás' homicide rate from 38.8 to 18.4 per 100,000 inhabitants between 2018 and 2024, while Zema lowered Minas Gerais' rate from 16.2 to 12.8 over the same period.

item.title: Como o TSE pode evitar a repetição dos excessos de 2022
item.description: The TSE has the opportunity to avoid the excesses of 2022 by adopting a minimalist and surgical approach, especially amid a potential rise in disinformation amplified by generative AI. While technologies like deepfakes and AI-driven candidate recommendations are prohibited and technically detectable, the greater challenge lies in judicial self-restraint to prevent the court from becoming a campaign protagonist, preserving the marketplace of ideas essential to democratic debate.

item.title: Pedro Rousseff x Nikolas Ferreira: os generais da guerra digital entre o PT e o PL
item.description: Pedro Rousseff, nephew of Dilma Rousseff and Belo Horizonte city councilor, has been appointed to lead the digital strategy for Lula’s 2026 campaign, tasked with countering virtual attacks against the president. He oversees a WhatsApp group called 'guerrilha' with over 400 government-aligned influencers. His main rival is Nikolas Ferreira, a federal deputy from PL and social media star with 43 million followers, known for derailing government initiatives with single posts.

item.title: Erika Hilton leva público a gritar “Fora, Alcolumbre” na Parada LGBT
item.description: Federal deputy Erika Hilton (PSOL-SP) led a crowd chanting 'Out, Alcolumbre' during São Paulo’s 30th LGBTQ+ Pride Parade, demanding a vote on ending the 6×1 work schedule. Speaking from the main sound truck on Avenida Paulista, she criticized Senate President Davi Alcolumbre (União Brasil-AP) for legislative inaction. The audience responded enthusiastically to the protest.

item.title: Jair Bolsonaro está perdendo seguidores na internet e enfrenta processo de ‘morte digital’
item.description: Jair Bolsonaro lost approximately 800,000 social media followers since late last year, dropping from 68.5 million to 67.7 million. This decline, attributed to his judicial ban from platforms and controversies involving his son Flávio Bolsonaro, is described as a 'digital death' process. While his sons, particularly Carlos Bolsonaro, continue to post in his defense, Bolsonaro's online absence weakens his public presence.

item.title: Lula posta vídeo em que faz exercícios sem camisa
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) posted a video of himself exercising shirtless, encouraging the public to prioritize health. At 80, he aims to live to 120 through his fitness routine and preventive medical treatments, including radiotherapy after skin cancer removal in April. First Lady Janja Lula da Silva shared a similar video the previous Thursday.

item.title: PREDIDENTE LULA VSI CRISTALIZANDO VITÓRIA NAS ELEIÇÕES 2026..
item.description: The content suggests that President Lula is consolidating an advantage in projections for the 2026 elections, with indications that his re-election is becoming increasingly likely despite political and economic challenges. The video, seemingly from a live broadcast or analysis, mentions that the narrative of victory is crystallizing, possibly due to relative government stability and opposition weakness. However, the provided excerpt contains irrelevant or duplicated elements (such as YouTube instructions), which obscure a clear reading of the central political context.

item.title: TCU arquiva representação de Flávio Bolsonaro sobre ex-nora de Lula por falta de 'indícios mínimos suficientes'
item.description: The TCU archived a representation by Senator Flávio Bolsonaro requesting an investigation into alleged undue favoritism toward Life Tecnologia Educacional, a company linked to Lula’s former daughter-in-law, due to insufficient evidence. The Court found the request relied solely on press articles without documentation to identify specific acts, contracts, or responsibilities. The ruling does not affect the ongoing PF investigation in the Coffe Break operation.

item.title: “Mais um problema do Lula”, diz Flávio sobre veto da UE à carne brasileira
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), a pre-candidate for president, criticized the European Union's veto on Brazilian exports of certain animal-origin products, blaming the Lula government and calling it 'another problem for Lula'. He shared his view in a post on social media platform X on Sunday, the 7th.

item.title: Bolsonaro disse em 2020 não saber o que era o Pix
item.description: On October 5, 2020, the day Pix registration began, Jair Bolsonaro said he did not know the Central Bank's instant payment system, confusing it with a civil aviation deregulation package. Although his official social media had previously mentioned Pix, he stated he would speak with Roberto Campos Neto, then BC president, to learn about it. This contrasts with Senator Flávio Bolsonaro’s current claim that his father created Pix, a system technically developed under Temer’s government and launched during Bolsonaro’s administration.

item.title: Libertou seus escravizados em 1883 e elegeu a primeira eleitora do Brasil: a segunda maior cidade potiguar virou referência para morar no interior no Nordeste
item.description: Mossoró, in Rio Grande do Norte, freed its enslaved people in 1883 — five years before the Lei Áurea — and hosted Brazil’s first female vote in 1927, in addition to expelling Lampião’s gang. These pioneering social and political milestones have established it as a reference for progressive living in the Northeast hinterland, attracting those seeking quality of life rooted in strong historical identity.

item.title: Governo Lula impõe sigilo sobre processos de autorização de bets
item.description: The Lula government has imposed secrecy, in some cases for up to 100 years, on the authorization processes of betting houses (bets) in Brazil, according to Estadão. The measure, linked to the Ministry of Finance, restricts public access to opinions, technical notes, and analyses related to the sector's regulation.

item.title: A 30ª Parada do Orgulho LGBT+ alerta sobre importância do voto
item.description: The 30th LGBT+ Pride Parade in São Paulo, held on Avenida Paulista, emphasized the importance of voting to secure rights through legislation, not just judicial rulings. Under the theme '30 Years of SP Pride Parade: The Street Calls, the Ballot Confirms,' the event recalled historic achievements like stable union recognition and the criminalization of LGBTphobia, which were later affirmed by the STF after street advocacy. APOLGBT-SP director Matheus Emílio Pereira da Silva stressed that legislative action is still needed to enshrine these rights in law.

item.title: Parada LGBT+ leva urna eletrônica “Votinho” para as ruas
item.description: The 30th São Paulo LGBTQ+ Pride Parade, held on June 7, 2026, featured an inflatable 'Votinho' ballot box mascot, referencing the TSE's 'Pilili' character, to promote the theme 'The street calls, the ballot confirms'. The event emphasized the link between street mobilization and electoral participation as complementary tools for advancing LGBTQIA+ rights, with appearances by PSOL legislators Erika Hilton and Sâmia Bomfim, while Guilherme Boulos was absent.

item.title: Casos Dark Horse e Master: as primeiras pistas de Nunes Marques como presidente do TSE
item.description: Minister Kassio Nunes Marques, appointed by Bolsonaro to the STF and currently president of the TSE, is the rapporteur in cases concerning the film Dark Horse and Flávio Bolsonaro’s ties to banker Daniel Vorcaro. The PL claims the AtlasIntel poll induced voter responses by including audio of Flávio’s conversation with Vorcaro, while the PT seeks to ban the film over alleged economic abuse. Despite Bolsonaro supporters anticipating favorable rulings, Nunes Marques has indicated a preference for a less interventionist approach in electoral justice.

item.title: Na Parada LGBT+, Erika diz que fim da 6 X 1 veio de travesti preta
item.description: Federal Deputy Erika Hilton (Psol-SP) stated that the progress on reducing the workweek from 6x1 to 5x2 was led by a 'Black trans woman', during her speech at the 30th São Paulo LGBT+ Pride Parade. She linked this labor victory to the presence of LGBT+ people in positions of power, arguing that the community drives change when it occupies institutional politics. Hilton urged the Senate to advance the 6x1 PEC and connected the workers' rights struggle to electoral engagement, echoing the parade's theme: 'the street calls, the ballot confirms'.

item.title: MPF abre inquérito para investigar falhas de fiscalização da Anac
item.description: The Federal Public Ministry (MPF) has opened an inquiry to investigate alleged failures and omissions in the oversight work of the National Civil Aviation Agency (Anac) under the Lula government. The investigation follows a federal budget block of R$24 million, which forced Anac to suspend 40% of its inspection activities, including pilot and flight attendant certifications, aircraft certifications, and technology investments, while also laying off contractors and canceling safety events. Anac warns that these measures directly threaten national air safety, reduce revenue, hinder new professional entry, and block the operation of new aircraft in Brazil.

item.title: Entenda por que o volante Éderson foi convocado para seleção brasileira no lugar do lateral-direito Wesley
item.description: Coach Carlo Ancelotti summoned midfielder Éderson to the Brazil squad for the 2026 World Cup after cutting right-back Wesley, favoring the player's versatility from his time playing on the flank for Atalanta. Éderson, 26, was included in Ancelotti's initial June 2025 list but did not play. The original right-back options considered were Paulo Henrique (Vasco) and Vitinho (Botafogo).

item.title: Quem é Éderson, volante que foi convocado para substituir Wesley na seleção brasileira
item.description: Midfielder Éderson, 26, has been called up to the Brazil national team to replace injured Wesley for the 2026 World Cup. He is a key player for Atalanta, with whom he won the 2023/24 Europa League, and is linked with a move to Manchester United.

item.title: TCU rejeita ação de Flávio Bolsonaro envolvendo ex-nora de Lula
item.description: The Federal Court of Accounts (TCU) dismissed a petition filed by Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) requesting an investigation into alleged irregularities in the Ministry of Education involving the company Life Tecnologia Educacional. The TCU determined there was insufficient evidence to proceed, rejecting the request based on Federal Police reports that mentioned Carla Ariane Trindade, former daughter-in-law of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.

item.title: TCU arquiva ação de Flávio para investigar empresa de ex-nora de Lula
item.description: The Federal Court of Accounts (TCU) dismissed a representation by Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) requesting an investigation into Life Tecnologia Educacional, a company linked to Carla Ariane Trindade, former daughter-in-law of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. The TCU concluded that the request lacked sufficient evidence, relying mainly on journalistic reports without concrete documents or proof of irregularities, and noted that ongoing investigations by the Federal Police are adequate to address the matter.

item.title: A nova aposta dos bolsonaristas para tentar livrar o ex-presidente da cadeia
item.description: Bolsonaro's defense is seeking to overturn his conviction through a criminal revision action at the STF, claiming weaknesses in the evidence and due process violations, without presenting new evidence. Senator Rogério Marinho, coordinator of Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign, reaffirmed confidence in the former president's innocence, even referencing past statements by Minister Luiz Fux as grounds for hope. Although the case is rapporteured by Kassio Nunes Marques, the bolsonarist strategy revives the 'in Fux we trust' narrative, linking the Vaza-Jato scandal to the current effort to reverse the sentence.

item.title: O lado de Donald Trump na eleição presidencial brasileira
item.description: In less than a week, Trump administration decisions affected Brazil, including designating PCC and CV as terrorist organizations and imposing new export tariffs of up to 37,5%. Flávio Bolsonaro celebrated the apparent Trump support and used it to claim superior security credentials, while Lula accused the Bolsonaro family of treason and revived national sovereignty rhetoric. Despite symbolic gestures, there is no clear evidence that Trump is actively seeking to influence the Brazilian election in favor of any candidate.

item.title: Dino manda retirar vídeo de candidato e critica “bizarrices e grosserias”
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Flávio Dino upheld an order to remove videos posted by Manaus city councilman Alexandre Salazar (PL) targeting former mayor and gubernatorial pre-candidate David Almeida (Avante). Dino criticized the content as containing 'bizarre and vulgar' remarks, emphasizing the need for respect in political discourse.

item.title: Alcione volta ao Maracanã e não desafina na presença de Lula
item.description: Alcione kicked off the 'O Maior Encontro do Samba' tour at Maracanã alongside Zeca Pagodinho and Jorge Aragão, with President Lula visiting Zeca's dressing room escorted by Marcelo Freixo. The show featured Martinho da Vila and announced upcoming special guests: Seu Jorge in Brasília (19/9), Alexandre Pires in Curitiba (7/11), Péricles in Porto Alegre (14/11), and Gilberto Gil in Belo Horizonte (28/11).

item.title: Brasil intensifica negociações para barrar veto da UE à carne
item.description: The Lula government is intensifying negotiations with the European Union to overturn a sanitary veto on Brazilian beef, set to take effect on September 3 and threatening R$9 billion in annual exports. The dispute centers on the EU’s demand for proof of cattle traceability and antimicrobial use compliance, with Brazil assessing whether it can exhaust its reduced-tariff quota before the deadline to lessen economic impact.

item.title: Dino critica 'bizarrices e grosserias' no discurso político e mantém remoção de vídeo com ofensas
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Flávio Dino upheld the removal of an offensive video by councilman Alexandre Salazar targeting David Almeida, labeling it as negative anticipatory electoral propaganda and criticizing the 'colonization of political discourse by bizarreness and vulgarity'. He stated that low-level language is not protected by parliamentary immunity, but allowed the future use of the slogan 'nunca será' in future posts, provided legal and ethical rules are followed, annulling the isolated fine for the expression while maintaining the obligation to remove strictly offensive content.
